get.description: Retrieve logs for all user's active applications.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Allowed values: any positive integer starting from 1.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Allowed values: any positive integer starting from 1.

parameters.name: filter:error
parameters.description: Possible values: true/false. Format: `?filters=[{"error":{"type": "=", "value":true}}]``

parameters.name: filter:applicationId
parameters.description: Possible values: one or several strings in array. Format: `?filters=[{"applicationId":{"type": "in", "value":["e1656509199c931911e919a00b1906ad1a26a450", "e1656509199c931911e919a00b1906ad1a26a451"]}}]`

parameters.name: filter:method
parameters.description: Possible values: array of strings. Format: `?filters=[{"method":{"type": "in", "value": "POST", "PUT]}}]`

parameters.name: filter:uri
parameters.description: Possible values: array of strings. Format: `?filters=[{"uri":{"type": "match", "value": "string"}}]` - finds only requests where the uri contains the value of the filter; `?filters=[{"uri":{"type": "like", "value": "user"}}]` - finds requests where the uri contains text from values of the filter.

parameters.name: filter:code
parameters.description: Possible values: array of two integers. Format: `?filters=[{"code":{"type": "between", "value": [0,500]}}]`

parameters.name: filter:time
parameters.description: Possible values: integer. Format: `?filters=[{"time":{"type": "=", "value": 2}}]`

parameters.name: filter:created
parameters.description: Possible values: two integers in array. Format: `?filters=[{"created":{"type": "between", "value": [1565360895, 1565360896]}}]`

parameters.name: sort:created
parameters.description: Sort results in ascending or descending order. Possible values: asc/desc. Format: `?sort[email]=asc`

200.description:
Returns request logs in case of successful response. Returns an error when:

User does not have an active subscription, "code": 0. Message: "User does not have active subscription"

get.description: Retrieve specific user log for an active application.

parameters.name: request_id
parameters.description: Can be retrieved from `GET /request-logs` request.

200.description:
Returns the request log in case of successful response. Returns an error when:

* Given {request_id} does not exist or user doesn't own this log, "code": 0. Message: "Request log with ID `{request_id}` not found"
* User does not have an active subscription, "code": 0. Message: "User does not have active subscription"

get.description: Retrieve logs of the paid requests.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Allowed values: any positive integer starting from 1.

parameters.name: filter:type
parameters.description: Possible values: 'free_form_invite', 'invite_to_sign', 'signing_link', 'document_group_invite', 'bulk_invite'. Format: `?filters=[{"type":{"type":"in","value":["free_form_invite"]}}]`

parameters.name: filter:date
parameters.description: Possible values: two integers in array or null. Format: `?filters=[{"date":{"type":"between","value":[null,100]}}]`

200.description:
Returns paid request logs in case of successful response. Returns an error when:

* User does not have an active subscription, "code": 0. Message: "User does not have active subscription"

get.description: Export logs of the paid requests in an XLSX file.

parameters.name: filter:date
parameters.description: Possible values: two UNIX timestamps in array or null. Format: `?filters=[{"date":{"type":"between","value":["2019-10-31","2019-10-31"]}}]`

parameters.name: filter:client_id
parameters.description: Possible values: client_id of the application to get paid request logs for. Format: `?filters=[{"client_id":{"type":"in","value":["{{client_id}}"]}}]`

200.description:
Returns an XLSX file in case of successful response. Returns an error when:

* Filter covers more than 90 days, "code": 0. Message: "The `date` filter gap should be 90 days or less."
* Request with invalid filter, "code": 0. Message: "Wrong filters format."
* User does not have an active subscription, "code": 0. Message: "User does not have active subscription"
* Request by the user whose bearer is generated by api dashboard app, "code": 200. empty xlsx file

get.description: Retrieve statistics about total used monthly requests during the subscription period.

200.description:
Returns monthly totals in case of successful response. Returns an error when:

* Request with expired subscription/user does not have subscription, "code": 0. Message: "User does not have active subscription"

get.description: Retrieve statistics about total, used, and remaining API limits.

200.description:
Returns total, used, and remaining API limits in case of successful response. Returns an error when:

* User doesn't have any API subscription plan, "code": 0. Message: "User does not have any API Plan"

get.description:
Allows users to get the list of webhook events (events history) by the subscription ID.

The results can be filtered and sorted. If the `sort` parameter is not indicated, the results are sorted by the `start_time` in descending order. The `filters` and `sort` parameters need URL-encoding.

parameters.name: subscription_id
parameters.description: ID of the subscription

parameters.name: sort:end_time
parameters.description: Sort results by the end time. Possible values: asc, desc. Format: `?sort[end_time]=desc`

parameters.name: sort:start_time
parameters.description: Sort results by the start time. Possible values: asc, desc. Format: `?sort[start_time]=desc`

parameters.name: sort:code
parameters.description: Sort results by the response code. Possible values: asc, desc. Format: `?sort[code]=desc`

parameters.name: filters:initiator_id
parameters.description: Search for a string in initiator IDs. Format: `?filters=[{"_OR":[{"initiator_id ":{"type":"like","value":"21a28b47"}}]}]`

parameters.name: filters:date
parameters.description: Filter results by the timestamps of start time. Format: `?filters=[{"date":{"type":"between","value":[1580719773,1580720509]}}]`

parameters.name: filters:code
parameters.description: Filter results by the response codes. Format: `?filters=[{"code":{"type": "between", "value":[199,299]}}]`

parameters.name: Content-Type
parameters.description: application/json

400.description:
* Token issue
* Incorrect filter format (each filter must contain `type` and `value` fields)
* Incorrect filter expression (must be a string)
* Incorrect `code` or `date` filter expression (must be `"type": "between"`)
* Incorrect `initiator_id` filter expression (must be `"type": "like"`)
* Incorrect `code` or `date` filter value (must be an array of 2 integers)
* Incorrect `initiator_id` filter value (must be a string)

errors.message: Incorrect filter format, filter must have `type` and `value` fields.
The `code` filter value must be of type array with 2 integer.
The `date` filter value must be of type array with 2 integer.
Incorrect filter format, filter `type` must be a string.
The `code` filter expression must be equal to `between`.
The `date` filter expression must be equal to `between`.
The `initiator_id` filter value must be a string.
The `initiator_id` filter expression must be equal to `like`.

* Request with non-existing subscription_id
* Request with invalid subscription_id

callback_url.description: URL to which the webhook payload was sent.

request_method.description: HTTP method used for the callback request. Always `post`.

metadata.description: Custom metadata attached to the entity at the time the event was triggered.

timestamp.description: Unix timestamp of when the event occurred.

access_token.description: Bearer access token. Present only if `delete_access_token` is `false`.

content.description: Event-specific payload. The fields vary depending on the event type. The parameters listed here correspond to the `document_group.invite.declined` and `user.document_group.invite.declined` events. See the response description for per-event payload examples.

request_content.description: Full payload sent to the callback URL.

request_headers.description: HTTP headers sent with the callback request.

application_name.description: Name of the application that owns the subscription.

request_end_time.description: Unix timestamp of when the request completed.

response_content.description: Response body returned by the callback URL.

request_start_time.description: Unix timestamp of when the request was initiated.

response_status_code.description: HTTP status code returned by the callback URL.

event_subscription_id.description: ID of the event subscription that triggered this callback.

event_subscription_active.description: Indicates whether the event subscription is currently active.

event_subscription_owner_email.description: Email of the user who owns the event subscription.

parameters.name: sort:code

parameters.name: sort:event
parameters.description: Sort results by the specific type of event (from A to Z). Possible values: asc, desc. Format: `?sort[event]=desc`

parameters.name: sort:application

post.description:
This endpoint allows users to import contacts from a CSV file into the authenticated user account. Users can map CSV columns to contact fields and configure how duplicate contacts are handled.

**Notes:**
* The CSV file must contain a header row. Data rows start from line 2.
* Rows where the email value is missing or invalid are skipped and reported under `failed`.
* Rows with invalid non-email fields (phone, address, etc.) are still created with those fields set to `null` and reported as `created_partial`.
* CSV separator is auto-detected from the header row (supported: `,`, `;`, `\t`, `|`).
* Phone country codes are auto-detected from the phone number format (e.g., `+1` → `US`, `+44` → `GB`).
* If `duplicates` is not specified and duplicate contacts (by email) already exist, a `409 Conflict` is returned.

**Sample CSV**

```csv
First Name,Last Name,Email,Phone,Company Name,Job Title,Country,Street Address,Apartment,City,State,ZIP Code,Description
John,Smith,john@example.com,5551234567,Sample Company,Manager,US,17 Station St,Suite 101,Brookline,Massachusetts,02445,This is a sample contact to demonstrate how the columns should be filled out. Don't forget to remove this contact before importing your contacts.
```

> Values in `mapping[...]` must exactly match the column headers in your CSV (case-sensitive, including spaces and punctuation). Set an optional `mapping[...]` to `null` to skip a field.

parameters.name: file
parameters.description: CSV file to import. Maximum size: 5 MB. Maximum rows: 3000 (excluding header).

parameters.name: duplicates
parameters.description: Duplicate handling strategy. Allowed values: `skip`, `replace`. If omitted, the request returns `409 Conflict` when contacts with matching emails already exist.

parameters.name: mapping[email]
parameters.description: Maps the contact email to a CSV column. The value is the column header name in your CSV. Required. Email values in the column must be valid and cannot end with `@no.reply`. Example value: `Email`.

parameters.name: mapping[first_name]
parameters.description: Maps the contact first name to a CSV column. The value is the column header name. Maximum 128 characters. Example value: `First Name`.

parameters.name: mapping[last_name]
parameters.description: Maps the contact last name to a CSV column. The value is the column header name. Maximum 128 characters. Example value: `Last Name`.

parameters.name: mapping[description]
parameters.description: Maps the contact description to a CSV column. The value is the column header name. Maximum 408 characters. Example value: `Description`.

parameters.name: mapping[phone]
parameters.description: Maps the contact phone number to a CSV column. The value is the column header name. Phone values must contain 10–15 digits; country code is auto-detected from the format. Example value: `Phone`.

parameters.name: mapping[company][name]
parameters.description: Maps the company name to a CSV column. The value is the column header name. Maximum 128 characters. Example value: `Company Name`.

parameters.name: mapping[company][job_title]
parameters.description: Maps the contact job title to a CSV column. The value is the column header name. Maximum 128 characters. Example value: `Job Title`.

parameters.name: mapping[address][country]
parameters.description: Maps the contact country to a CSV column. The value is the column header name. Country values must use ISO 2-character codes. Required when `mapping[address][zip_code]` is provided. Example value: `Country`.

parameters.name: mapping[address][street]
parameters.description: Maps the street address to a CSV column. The value is the column header name. Maximum 255 characters. Example value: `Street Address`.

parameters.name: mapping[address][apartment]
parameters.description: Maps the apartment / unit to a CSV column. The value is the column header name. Maximum 255 characters. Example value: `Apartment`.

parameters.name: mapping[address][city]
parameters.description: Maps the city to a CSV column. The value is the column header name. Maximum 128 characters. Example value: `City`.

parameters.name: mapping[address][state]
parameters.description: Maps the state to a CSV column. The value is the column header name. United States only. Maximum 128 characters. Example value: `State`.

parameters.name: mapping[address][zip_code]
parameters.description: Maps the zip code to a CSV column. The value is the column header name. Maximum 10 characters. Requires `mapping[address][country]` to be provided. Example value: `ZIP Code`.

rows.description: Row numbers (starting at 2) of failed rows.

failed.description: Rows that could not be created due to a missing or incorrect email.

created.description: Number of contacts fully created (excludes partially created).

created_partial.description: Contacts created with some non-email fields set to `null` due to validation errors.

post.description:
This endpoint allows users to send a document invite with a payment request. Recipients will be redirected to the payment page after completing the documents. > To request a payment, users must either connect to the payment service individually or accept an invitation to an organization already connected to the payment service. - To invite a user to an organization, see [Add members](/docs/organization/operations/post-v2-organizations-org-id-members). - To accept an invitation to an organization, the user can click the link they receive, or see [Accept invite to organization](/docs/organization/operations/post-v2-organizations-org-id-members-user-id-accept). - To connect your organization to the payment service, see [Connect to merchant account](/docs/request-payments/operations/post-organizations-org-id-merchantaccount). A payment request can be linked to a specific field (`calculated` type) or set as a fixed amount (`fixed`type). This article lists only the parameters required for a payment request. For other field invite parameters, see [Send field invite](/docs/document-field-invite/operations/post-document-doc-id-invite).
**Use additional attributes to customize the request** | Parameter | Description | Example | | --- | --- | --- | | `field_type` | Type of the field that sets the payment amount. Required if the request `type` is `calculated`. For a payment request invite, `filed_type` is `text_fields`. | | | `field_name` | Name of the field that sets the payment amount. Used if the `type` is `calculated`. Can be found in the [Get document response](/docs/document/operations/get-document) (fields.name). | See the screenshot above. | | `type` | Defines how the payment amount is set. Allowed values: `fixed` (the amount is set in the amount field) and `calculated` (set using a document field).

Learn how to [add a payment request field](/docs/request-payments/operations/put-document-document-id). | | | `currency` | Payment currency in ISO format. | | | `amount` | Amount of payment. Required if `type` is 'fixed'. | See the screenshot above. |

post.description:
This endpoint allows users to create an embedded signing invite for a document group. Once the invite is created, generate an embedded signing link using [`POST /document-groups/{{document_group_id}}/embedded-invites/{{embedded_invite_id}}/link`](/docs/doc-group-embedded-signing/operations/generate-link-for-embedded-invite-document-group) with the ID you got in the response. Before sending your request, ensure the following: * You are the owner of the document group to be signed. * Every document in the payload is a part of a document group. * The document group contains at least one document. * The document group is not part of any other invite (pending or signed). * At least one document in the document group contains fields. * Signers' email addresses are unique and do not exceed 150 characters. * All roles or role IDs in the document group are included in the invite (specifying extra roles will result in an error). **Action types** in `documents`: * `sign`: the recipient signs the document. * `view`: the recipient views the document. * `approve`: the recipient approves the document without signing or filling fields. Only one approver is allowed per invite step, the step must not include other actions, and all document IDs in the document group must be listed for the approver. Parameters `role` and `role_id` can be retrieved from the response from [`GET /document/{{document_id}}`](/docs/document/operations/get-document). Specify a role either by `role` (unique role name, e.g. “Signer 1”), `role_id` (unique role identifier), or both `role` and `role_id`. Ensure they correspond to each other. Use these parameters to customize the request:
Recipient authentication for the signing session Use the `authentication` object to set up the signer's authentication for the signing session. * Authentication type: `phone`, method: `sms`. Note that `sms_message` parameter must contain `{password}` placeholder. This method is used to authenticate the signer using a password sent via SMS. ```json "authentication": { "type": "phone", "method": "sms", "phone": "+1XXXXXXXXX", "sms_message": "Custom test message with {password}" } ``` * Authentication type: `phone`, method: `phone_call` This method is used to authenticate the signer with a password delivered via a phone call. ```json "authentication": { "type": "phone", "method": "phone_call", "phone": "+1XXXXXXXXX" } ``` * Authentication type: `password` This method is used to authenticate the signer using a pre-set password. ```json "authentication": { "type": "password", "password": "123456" } ```

auth_method used in the integrated application The `auth_method` parameter is defined by the application owner to specify the method used to authenticate the recipient (signer or approver) within the integrated application. Possible values are: `password`, `email`, `social`, `mfa`, `biometric`, `other`, `none`. **Note**: The `auth_method` parameter does not influence the recipient's authentication method during the signing or approval session. Use the `authentication` object to configure authentication for the session.

from_email, from_name Use `from_email` and `from_name` parameters to customize the appearance of the sender's email address and name. Note that both parameters are optional and applicable only when `delivery_type`=`email`. Explore the three scenarios of passing the `from_name` and `from_email` parameters: **When both `from_email` and `from_name` are passed:** The custom `from_name` appears: - in email subject of the invite, reassign, reminder, and completed emails. The custom `from_email` appears: - in email body of the invite, reassign, reminder, and completed emails. - when clicking **Contact Sender** and in **Reply-to** in the emails. - in the signing session: when clicking **Contact Sender** in the **More Actions** menu. --- **When only `from_email` is passed:** The local part of `from_email` (before `@`) appears: - in email subject of the invite, reassign, reminder, and completed emails. The custom `from_email` appears: - in email body of the invite, reassign, reminder, and completed emails. - when clicking **Contact Sender** and in **Reply-to** in the emails. - in the signing session: when clicking **Contact Sender** in the **More Actions** menu. --- **When only `from_name` is passed:** The custom `from_name` appears: - in email subject of the invite, reassign, reminder, and completed emails. The default (owner’s) `from_email` appears: - in email body of the invite, reassign, reminder, and completed emails. - when clicking **Contact Sender** and in **Reply-to** in the emails. - in the signing session: when clicking **Contact Sender** in the **More Actions** menu.
Learn more about [embedded signing](/docs/guides-embedded-signing).

put.description:
This endpoint allows users to add or remove document group recipients. Users can edit recipients' emails, roles and role actions, signing order, CC recipients, and more. 

You cannot edit recipients for a document group with an active signature invite.

> To pre-fill recipients' information when sending an invite, `name` must match `role`.

**Recipients and roles in document groups**

- The same email address can have multiple roles in a document group — for example, if the recipient acts as "Agent" in one document and "Manager" in another.
- The API creates a separate entry for each role, so the same email address may appear multiple times in the response.

**Example:** If recipient@example.com is assigned as "Agent" in Document A and "Manager" in Document B, the response will contain two separate entries for recipient@example.com — one per role.

**Mapping tip:** When mapping recipients in your integration, group by email address rather than by role name.

get.description:
This endpoint returns document group invite information, including the status of each field invite, step and action.

Here is the list of possible invite, action and step statuses:
- `created`: invite, action, or step has been created but is not waiting to be signed.
- `pending`: emails have been sent out for this invite action or step and are waiting to be viewed or signed.
- `fulfilled`: the invite, action, or step has been completed by signing, viewing or approving.
- `correction`: the step recipient is modifying the invite. 
- `canceled`: the invite or step has been canceled by the recipient.

Possible invite actions are:
- `view`: The recipient can only review the document without making changes.
- `sign`: The recipient can sign or fill out the document.
- `approve`: The recipient can review the document to approve or decline it.

post.description:
This endpoint allows users to create an invite for signing a document group. You can configure a multistep workflow, where different recipients act on the document group at different stages. Recipients can receive the invite by email or by SMS: identify a recipient by `email` for email delivery or by `phone_invite` for SMS delivery. You can combine email and SMS recipients in a single request. For more information, see the [SMS invite guide](/docs/sms-invite). Each invite step includes: - `order`: the sequence number of the step. - `invite_actions`: an array of objects specifying who is invited and the action they must perform: - **`sign`**: The recipient can sign or fill out the document. - **`approve`**: The recipient can review the document to approve or decline it. - **`view`**: The recipient can only review the document without making changes. - `invite_emails`: an array for customizing the emails sent to recipients at that step. - `invite_sms`: an array for customizing the SMS invites sent to recipients at that step: custom SMS text (`sms_message`), expiration, and reminder settings. Once all invite actions in a step are completed, the system sends the emails or SMS messages for the next step. When all steps are complete, completion emails are triggered. To invite a **signing group**, use the `email_groups` field. A signing group includes multiple email addresses, and the step is marked complete as soon as any member of the group signs. You can either use an existing group or define a new one by providing a 40-character ID, a group name, and the list of recipient emails. To create a signing group separately, see [Create contact group](/docs/contact-groups/operations/post-v2-crm-groups). Learn more about an [Invite to sign a document group](/docs/invite-to-sign#send-a-document-group-for-signature).
**Use additional attributes to customize signing experience** Parameter | Description | Example ---------|----------|--------- `reassign` | A recipient can forward the invite by clicking **More Actions** > **Forward Invite** and entering an email address. | `force_new_signature` | A recipient must create a new signature for each signature field. | `prefill_signature_name` | A string with a signature name that appears when a signer clicks a signature field. The signer can edit the signature.| `required_preset_signature_name` | A string with a signature name that appears when a signer clicks a signature field. The signer cannot edit the signature. | `decline_by_signature` | When a signer clicks a signature field, they see two options: sign the fields and decline the document group. | `authentication_type` | Requires a recipient to enter a password or a code before viewing the document group. For more information, see [Two-factor authentication](/docs/two-factor-authentication). |

The link to the document group and an opt-out notice are automatically added at the end of the SMS. Without this parameter, the recipient receives the default message: "{sender email} has sent you a document. Follow the link to view the document". Custom SMS messages require an API free trial, an active API subscription, or a Site License.

invite_emails.description: Objects that define custom email subject, email message, expiration and reminder settings for each recipient within a step.

email.description: Recipient's email address. The invite is delivered by email. Identify each recipient by `email`, `phone_invite`, or `email_group` — only one of these parameters at a time.

action.description: Allowed action with a document. Possible values: `view`, `sign`, `approve`. The `approve` action must be assigned to all documents in the document group. The `view` action can be assigned to any subset of documents in the group.

language.description: Sets the language of the signing session and notification emails for the signer. Possible values: `en` for English, `es` for Spanish, and `fr` for French. If not set, the language is determined by the language of your signNow account. If emails are branded, you can set up [your own](/docs/guides-branding#language-branding) email texts in different languages.

role_name.description: Recipient's role name in the document (can be used to identify fields in the document assigned to this particular recipient). The `role` parameter is also supported as an equivalent of `role_name`.

type.description: Type of QES signature. Possible values: `eideasy`,` eideasy-pdf`, and `nom151`. All signers in the invite must have the same signature type.

signature.description:
This object is used to request QES signatures from signers. To use it, a user must be a member of an organization (workspace) with QES settings enabled. If QES is used, it must be used for all signers in the invite.
For more information, see [QES user guide](/docs/qualified-electronic-signature).

document_id.description: ID of the document on which actions are required from this recipient.

name.description: The name of the contact group.

email_group.description: A contact group of recipients, for example, [CRM Contact group](/docs/contact-groups/operations/post-v2-crm-groups).

phone_invite.description: Recipient's phone number. The invite is delivered by SMS instead of email. Use instead of `email`. To customize the SMS text, expiration, or reminders, add an object with the same phone number to the `invite_sms` array of this step.

redirect_uri.description: The link that opens after the recipient completes the document.

allow_reassign.description: Whether or not to allow recipients reassign this invite to another email address. Possible values: "0" - not allowed, "1" - allowed.

type.description: Type of signer's identity verification. Possible values: `"password"` or `"phone"`.

phone.description: Required in case of `"type"`: `"phone"`. User's phone number.

value.description: Required in case of `"type"`: `"password"`. The password for user authentication.

method.description: Required in case of `"type"`: `"phone"`. Possible values: `"phone_call`", `"sms"`.

message.description: In case of `"method"`: `"sms"` - custom SMS message, max 140 characters. Customizing the 2FA SMS message requires an API free trial, an active API subscription, or a Site License.

authentication.description: Object that contains the type of signer's identity verification, phone number or password.

type.description: In this case, must be "fixed".

merchant_id.description: The ID of the merchant account added to your organization (workspace).

payment_request.description: Object that contains details about the payment request.

redirect_target.description: Determines whether to open the redirect link in the new tab in the browser, or in the same tab after the signing session. Possible values: `blank` - opens the link in the new tab, `self` - opens the link in the same tab.

close_redirect_uri.description: The link that opens when a signer clicks **Save Progress and Finish Later** during a signing session or **Close** in view mode. Available for `sign ` action.

decline_by_signature.description: Whether or not to allow recipients decline to sign the invite.

decline_redirect_uri.description: The URL that opens after the recipient declines the document. Available for `sign` action.

prefill_signature_name.description: The text displayed in the Signature field. The signer can edit this value.

is_close_redirect_canceled.description: Specifies whether the save progress redirect setting is canceled for the organization (workspace).`true` – the redirect is canceled;`false` – the redirect remains active.

is_finish_redirect_canceled.description: Specifies whether the completion redirect setting is canceled for the organization (workspace).`true` – the redirect is canceled;`false` – the redirect remains active.

is_decline_redirect_canceled.description: Specifies whether the decline redirect setting is canceled for the organization (workspace).`true` – the redirect is canceled;`false` – the redirect remains active.

required_preset_signature_name.description: The text displayed in the Signature field. The signer cannot edit this value. Cannot be used simultaneously with `prefill_signature_name` or `force_new_signature` for the same role.

invite_actions.description: Objects that define recipients (email addresses, phone numbers for SMS delivery, or signing groups) and invite actions, roles and documents assigned to each recipient within a step.

invite_steps.description: Steps of the document group invite. Every step contains the `order` number, `invite_emails`, `invite_sms`, and `invite_actions` within this step.

sign_as_merged.description: If true, allows API user to send an invite which opens as merged document group in a single document.

client_timestamp.description: The timestamp of the document group invite.

remind_after.description: Days after invite is sent before a reminder is delivered. Must be less than `general_expiration_days`.

remind_before.description: Days before expiration when a reminder is delivered. Must be less than `general_expiration_days`.

general_reminder.description: Default `reminder` applied to all recipients in the invite.

email.description: Email address of the completion email recipient.

message.description: Custom message for the completion email. Requires a paid API plan, an API free trial, or a Site License.

subject.description: Custom subject for the completion email. Requires a paid API plan, an API free trial, or a Site License.

disable_document_attachment.description: Whether to disable sending document attachments with the completion email. Possible values: 0 - enable document attachment, 1 - disable document attachment.

completion_emails.description: Object that contains email addresses and custom settings for sending emails about completing the invite.

general_expiration_days.description: Default `expiration_days` applied to all recipients in the invite. Min: `1`, Max: `180`. Default: `30`.

general_expiration_time.description: Default expiration timestamp (Unix time, seconds) applied to all recipients in the invite.

id.description: ID of the created document group invite.

pending_invite_link.description: Link for signers with pending invites.

post.description: Cancels a group invite. All documents will be unshared with invitees. Any signatures that occurred before canceling will remain on the documents.

This endpoint either replaces the recipient at a particular invite step or updates the invite attributes (reminder, expiration, language) for a recipient at that step.

Recipients can be identified and replaced by email or by SMS. Identify the current recipient by `user_to_update` (email) or `phone_invite_to_update` (phone number). Set the new recipient with `replace_with_this_user` (email) or `replace_with_this_phone_invite` (phone number). This supports all four conversions: email to email, email to phone, phone to email, and phone to phone. For SMS invites, see the [SMS invite guide](/docs/sms-invite).

To get the current SMS recipient's phone number for `phone_invite_to_update`, call [Get doc group invite](/docs/doc-group-field-invite/operations/get-document-group-invite) and read `actions[].signer_phone_invite`.

**Notes**

* Send both an identifier and a replacement. Use one identifier (`user_to_update` for email or `phone_invite_to_update` for phone) and one replacement (`replace_with_this_user` for email or `replace_with_this_phone_invite` for phone). To keep the same recipient and only change attributes, repeat the current value in the replacement field.
* For an SMS recipient, omitting `replace_with_this_phone_invite` still returns `200`, but the invite stops being delivered, so always send it.
* When replacing with an email recipient, `invite_email.email` must equal `replace_with_this_user`. When replacing with an SMS recipient, `invite_sms.phone_invite` must equal `replace_with_this_phone_invite`.
* `update_invite_action_attributes` is optional. If omitted, every document the recipient has in the step is updated; if provided, only the listed `document_id`s are updated.
* `expiration_days` accepts `1` to `180`. `0` means use the organization's default invite-expiration setting (falls back to `30` days).
* A phone recipient is rejected when the `CFR` or `require_login_for_signing` setting is enabled. SMS delivery may still be suppressed after a `200` if the recipient has opted out of or declined SMS consent.
* `allow_reassign` cannot be combined with `replace_with_this_phone_invite`.
* With `is_short_link_invite: true` the service generates the recipient, so neither `replace_with_this_user` nor `replace_with_this_phone_invite` may be sent.

post.description:
This endpoint allows API users to create and send a FreeForm invite to sign a document group.

**FreeForm invite**

A FreeForm invite is an invite with a document that does not contain fields; recipients can add their signature anywhere on the document.
> A FreeForm invite can be sent to the sender's own email address.

**Schedule a freeform invite**

To send a FreeForm document group invite at a later time, use the [Schedule document group invite](/docs/scheduled-doc-group-invite/operations/post-document-group-scheduled-invite) endpoint with `is_freeform_invite: true`.

parameters.name: document_group_id
parameters.description: ID of the document group.

cc.description: Array with the list of CC email addresses.

email.description: Signer's email address. **Note**: A FreeForm invite can be sent to the sender's own email address.

language.description: Sets the language of the signing session and notification emails for the signer. Possible values: `en` for English, `es` for Spanish, and `fr` for French. If not set, the language is determined by the language of your SignNow account. get.description:
This endpoint allows API users to retrieve the details of a document.

The **Document** object contains:
* Metadata: file name, size, extension, and ID
* Fields, texts, checks, and signatures
* Invites and their statuses (available statuses are: `created`, `pending`, `fulfilled`, `canceled`, `skipped`)
* Roles:
  - Recipients with a sign action appear in the `roles` array.
  - Recipients with an approve action appear in the `approver_roles` array.
  - Recipients with a view action appear in the `viewer_roles` array.
* Timestamps (date created, and date updated)
* Document group information
* Document group template information
* Originator's organization-level settings
* Integrations settings
* Signing session settings
* Share information
  - `is_team_shared`: Returns `true`, if the file has been shared with a team. 
  - `role`: Indicates the user's access to the document: Allowed values are `sender`, `viewer`, or `owner`. 
  - `is_personally_shared_to_others`: Returns `true` if the template has been personally shared with other users (via the **Share** button). The attribute is visible to the template owner and users with access rights.


Document is a fundamental object of every eSignature workflow.

* To send an invite, select or [upload a document](/docs/document/operations/upload-document).
* When the document is signed, it can be [downloaded in PDF file format](/docs/document/operations/download-document).
* Documents in SignNow can be [turned into templates](/docs/template/operations/create-template).
* API also allows you to create [event subscriptions](/docs/basic-auth/operations/create-event-subscription) triggered by a specific document.

post.description:
This endpoint allows users to upload a document with text tags. Text tags can be of two types: simple and complex. **Simple text tags** use curly brackets and a notation system to define fields. **Complex text tags** use only field names on a document; field details are provided separately in the `Tags` array. > Only .doc, .docx, and .pdf formats are supported. **Additional parameters** `parse_type`: determines how the document text tags are parsed. Possible values: - `tag`: parse only simple tags. All Adobe (fillable) fields will be removed from the document without saving. - `adobe`: parse only Adobe (fillable) fields. All simple tags will be removed from the document without saving. - `all`: parse both simple tags and Adobe (fillable) fields. Also parses simple tags added inside Adobe fields as their content. - `default` (or if `parse_type` not specified): parse simple and complex tags and Adobe (fillable) fields. Simple tags added as the content of Adobe fields will not be parsed. For more information, see the [Text tags](/docs/text-tags) guide or check out our video tutorials:
**Simple text tags video tutorial** Note: The design shown in the video is outdated, but the flow is still accurate. You can go ahead and follow the steps as demonstrated. [Simple text tags video tutorial](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iopDT5_4-Co)

post.description:
This endpoint allows API users to share documents with one or more users. For each document-email pair, assign a `viewer` or `sender` role.

**Notes**

* **Viewer** - can view and download the document; **sender** - can view, download, invite to sign, and manage document invites.
* Only documents owned by the authenticated user may be shared.
* If the recipient already has access, their role is updated to the value sent in the request.
* The recipient receives an email notification with a link to the shared document.
* If the recipient does not exist in the system, a new account is created automatically.
* The document owner's email must not appear among the recipients.
* Documents belonging to a document group cannot be shared individually.
* Documents created from a template already shared with the target user are rejected with a conflict error.

**Request limits:** At most **100 distinct recipient emails** and **20 distinct documents** per request.

message.description: Custom message to include in the notification email.

get.description:
This endpoint allows API users to retrieve detailed information about a specific document group, including its documents, assigned roles, field and FreeForm invites, share info, owner details, and originator organization settings.

Available to the document group owner and to any user invited on any step, regardless of the current invite or step status.

**Notes**

* Use the `include` query parameter to add optional data to the response. To request several values, separate them with commas, for example `?include=documents.fields,reminder`. Unknown values are ignored.
* With `?include=documents.fields`, each item in `documents` contains a `fields` array. Without it, the response doesn't include `fields`, so existing integrations are not affected.
* The objects in `fields` have the same format as the `fields` array of [`GET /document/{document_id}`](/docs/document/operations/get-document) and cover all field types it returns.
* The response doesn't include dropdown options (`enumeration_options`) or checkbox groups (`checkbox_groups`). [`GET /document/{document_id}`](/docs/document/operations/get-document) returns them at the document level, so call it for each document that needs them.
* To add or update fields, call [`PUT /document/{document_id}`](/docs/document/operations/edit-document) for each document.

parameters.name: include=document_group_attributes
parameters.description: If used, the response will contain document group attributes.

parameters.name: include=reminder
parameters.description: If used, the response includes `general_expiration_time`, `general_expiration_days`, and `general_reminder` — defaults applied to all recipients in the invite.

parameters.name: include=documents.fields
parameters.description: If used, each item in `documents` contains a `fields` array with the fields of that document.

parameters.name: include=documents.freeform_invites
parameters.description: If used, each item in `documents` contains a `freeform_invites` array with the FreeForm invites sent for that document.

parameters.name: include=documents.signatures
parameters.description: If used, each item in `documents` contains a `signatures` array with the signatures added to that document.

parameters.name: include=entity_labels
parameters.description: If used, the response contains `entity_labels`: the labels assigned to the document group.

parameters.name: include=origin_dgt
parameters.description: If used, the response contains `origin_dgt`: the document group template the document group was created from.

parameters.name: include=recently_used
parameters.description: If used, the response contains `recently_used`: the Unix timestamp of the last activity on the document group.

parameters.name: document_group_id
parameters.description: ID of the document group.

get.description:
This endpoint allows API users to retrieve information about a specific document group template, including its documents, the roles assigned to each document, and, optionally, the fields in each document.

Available to the document group template owner and to users the template is shared with.

**Notes**

* Use the `include` query parameter to add optional data to the response. Unknown values are ignored.
* With `?include=documents.fields`, each item in `documents` contains a `fields` array. Without it, the response doesn't include `fields`.
* The objects in `fields` have the same format as the `fields` array of [`GET /document/{document_id}`](/docs/document/operations/get-document). Template fields don't contain a `data` key. Default values set in the template, such as `prefilled_text` for text fields, are returned inside `json_attributes`.
* The response doesn't include dropdown options (`enumeration_options`) or checkbox groups (`checkbox_groups`). [`GET /document/{document_id}`](/docs/document/operations/get-document) returns them at the document level, so call it for each document that needs them.
* `roles` contains role names only. To get the signing order and other recipient settings, call [`GET /v2/document-group-templates/{document_group_template_id}/recipients`](/docs/document-group-template/operations/get-v2-document-group-templates-doc-group-template-id-recipients).
* To add or update fields, call [`PUT /document/{document_id}`](/docs/document/operations/edit-document) for each document.
* To work with a document in the template, call this endpoint to get the current document IDs right before you use them.
* For document groups, use [`GET /v2/document-groups/{document_group_id}`](/docs/document-group/operations/get-document-group-info-v2).

parameters.name: include=documents.fields

post.description:
This endpoint allows API users to create a document group from a document group template.

The new document group is a signable copy: the template stays untouched as the master version. The documents in the group have new IDs that differ from the ones in the template, so build any invite from the IDs returned by this request. For the full flow, from preparing the documents to sending the group for signature, see [Documents, doc groups, and templates](/docs/entities). To let recipients sign the group inside your own site or app, see [Embedded signing](/docs/guides-embedded-signing).

This endpoint allows API users to create a new document group template from a document group in any status.

As a result, user gets one document group template and separate templates from each document in the document group.

post.description:
This endpoint allows users to create an embedded signing invite for a document. Once the invite is created, generate an embedded signing link using [`POST v2/documents/{{document_id}}/embedded-invites/{{embedded_invite_id}}/link`](/docs/document-embedded-signing/operations/generate-link-for-embedded-invite) with the ID you got in the response. Before sending your request, ensure the following: - You are the owner of the document to be signed. - The invite is being created for a document (not a template). - Your document contains fields. - The document is not part of any other invite (pending or signed). - Signers' email addresses are unique and do not exceed 150 characters. - All roles or role IDs in the document are included in the invite (specifying extra roles will result in an error). - The document owner cannot be assigned as a signer. You can also include `approvers`. These recipients review the document without signing or filling fields. Each approver requires `email`, `role`, `order`, and `auth_method`. Note that `order` values must be unique across `invites` and `approvers`. Parameters `role` and `role_id` can be retrieved from the response from [`GET /document/{{document_id}}`](/docs/document/operations/get-document). Specify a role either by `role` (unique role name, e.g. “Signer 1”), `role_id` (unique role identifier), or both `role` and `role_id`. Ensure they correspond to each other. Use these parameters to customize the request:
Recipient authentication for the signing session Use the `authentication` object to set up the signer's authentication for the signing session. * Authentication type: `phone`, method: `sms`. Note that `sms_message` parameter must contain `{password}` placeholder. This method is used to authenticate the signer using a password sent via SMS. ```json "authentication": { "type": "phone", "method": "sms", "phone": "+1XXXXXXXXX", "sms_message": "Custom test message with {password}" } ``` * Authentication type: `phone`, method: `phone_call` This method is used to authenticate the signer with a password delivered via a phone call. ```json "authentication": { "type": "phone", "method": "phone_call", "phone": "+1XXXXXXXXX" } ``` * Authentication type: `password` This method is used to authenticate the signer using a pre-set password. ```json "authentication": { "type": "password", "password": "123456" } ```

name_formula parameter Use the `name_formula` parameter to generate a completed document name based on the `text_prefix` (can be any text) and fillable field data. For example, let's set the first part of the completed document name as `Contract` and use data from two document fields (we can use up to five fields): * `signer_name` (filled as `John Smith`) * `signed_date` (filled as `20.01.2023`) After the signer completes the document, the document will have the name `Contract John Smith 20.01.2023`. Note that you can not use signature fields for `name_formula`.

auth_method used in the integrated application The `auth_method` parameter is defined by the application owner to specify the method used to authenticate the signer within the integrated application. Possible values are: `password`, `email`, `social`, `mfa`, `biometric`, `other`, `none`. **Note**: The `auth_method` parameter does not influence the signer's authentication method during the signing session. Use the `authentication` object to configure authentication for the signing session.

from_email, from_name Use `from_email` and `from_name` parameters to customize the appearance of the sender's email address and name. Note that both parameters are optional and applicable only when `delivery_type`=`email`. Explore the three scenarios of passing the from_name and from_email parameters: **When both `from_email` and `from_name` are passed:** The custom `from_name` appears: - in email subject of the invite, reassign, reminder, and completed emails. The custom `from_email` appears: - in email body of the invite, reassign, reminder, and completed emails. - when clicking **Contact Sender** and in **Reply-to** in the emails. - in the signing session: when clicking **Contact Sender** in the **More Actions** menu. --- **When only `from_email` is passed:** The local part of `from_email` (before `@`) appears: - in email subject of the invite, reassign, reminder, and completed emails. The custom `from_email` appears: - in email body of the invite, reassign, reminder, and completed emails. - when clicking **Contact Sender** and in **Reply-to** in the emails. - in the signing session: when clicking **Contact Sender** in the **More Actions** menu. --- **When only `from_name` is passed:** The custom `from_name` appears: - in email subject of the invite, reassign, reminder, and completed emails. The default (owner’s) `from_email` appears: - in email body of the invite, reassign, reminder, and completed emails. - when clicking **Contact Sender** and in **Reply-to** in the emails. - in the signing session: when clicking **Contact Sender** in the **More Actions** menu.
Learn more about [embedded signing](/docs/guides-embedded-signing).

post.description:
This endpoint allows users to send a document for signature via SMS. Recipients receive an SMS with a link to the document. It is the same `POST /document/{document_id}/invite` request as [Invite to sign](/docs/document-field-invite/operations/post-document-doc-id-invite), with signers identified by `phone_invite`. Different signers of one invite can receive it by SMS or by email.

Learn more about [SMS invites](/docs/sms-invite).

**Notes**

* SMS delivery is available for signers in the `to` array. Viewers and approvers receive the invite by email.
* Identify each signer by exactly one of `phone_invite`, `email`, or `email_group`.
* Use `sms_message` to customize the SMS text. `subject`, `message`, and `header` in `to` apply only to signers invited by email.
* `subject` and `message` in the request root are allowed when at least one signer receives the invite by email.
* `phone_invite` is `+` followed by digits, max `14` characters.
* SMS invites require the CFR and **Require login to sign** organization settings to be off, and cannot be used with `sso_login` authentication. See the errors in the `400` response.
* Custom `sms_message` and `authentication_sms_message` require an API free trial, an active API subscription, or a Site License.

parameters.name: Content-type
parameters.description: application/json

parameters.name: doc_id_for_sms
parameters.description: ID of the document. The same `document_id` as in [Invite to sign](/docs/document-field-invite/operations/post-document-doc-id-invite).

cc.description: Email addresses of CC recipients. Each address must be unique.

role.description: Signer's role name, for example `Signer 1`. Required unless `role_id` is specified.

email.description: Signer's email address for an email invite. Use exactly one of `email`, `phone_invite`, or `email_group` per signer.

order.description: Order of signing: `1` - the signer signs the document first, then the document is sent to `2`, `3`, and so on. Several signers can have the same order. Min: `1`, Max: `127`.

phone.description: Phone number used to verify the signer. Required with `"authentication_type": "phone"`.

method.description: Method of the `phone` authentication type. Required with `"authentication_type": "phone"`. Possible values: `sms`, `phone_call`.

message.description: Custom email message for the signer. Not allowed for signers invited by SMS. Requires a paid API plan, an API free trial, or a Site License.

role_id.description: ID of the signer's role. Can be used instead of `role`.

subject.description: Custom email subject for the signer. Not allowed for signers invited by SMS. Requires a paid API plan, an API free trial, or a Site License.

language.description: Language of the signing session and notification emails for the signer. Possible values: `en`, `es`, `fr`. If not set, the language of your SignNow account is used. If emails are branded, you can set up [your own](/docs/guides-branding#language-branding) email texts in different languages.

password.description: Password used to verify the signer. Required with `"authentication_type": "password"`.

reassign.description: Specifies whether the signer can forward the invite to another email address. `0` - signer cannot forward the invite, `1` - signer can forward the invite. Cannot be used with `email_group`.

remind_after.description: Days after the invite is sent before a reminder is delivered. Must be less than `expiration_days`.

remind_before.description: Days before expiration when a reminder is delivered. Must be less than `expiration_days`.

type.description: Type of QES signature. Possible values: `eideasy`,` eideasy-pdf`, and `nom151`. All signers in the invite must have the same signature type.

signature.description:
This object is used to request QES signatures from signers. To use it, a user must be a member of an organization with QES settings enabled. If QES is used, it must be used for all signers in the invite.
For more information, see [QES user guide](/docs/qualified-electronic-signature).

name.description: A name of the email group. Must be defined in the `email_groups` array.

email_group.description: A group of users that should receive the invite. When one of the users signs the document, the document is completed. Must be used with the `email_groups` array. Use exactly one of `email`, `phone_invite`, or `email_group` per signer. Cannot be used with `reassign`.

sms_message.example: Hi, here is a document for signature from {sender_email}
sms_message.description: Custom text of the SMS invite, max `230` characters. Only GSM-7 characters are allowed. Supports the `{sender_email}` placeholder, which is replaced with the sender's email address. The link to the document and an opt-out notice are added at the end of the SMS automatically. Without this parameter, the signer receives the default message: "{sender_email} has sent you a document. Follow the link to view the document". Used only for signers invited by SMS. Requires an API free trial, an active API subscription, or a Site License.

phone_invite.description: Signer's phone number for an SMS invite: `+` followed by digits, max `14` characters. Use exactly one of `email`, `phone_invite`, or `email_group` per signer. decline_by_signature.description: Specifies whether the signer can decline the invite by clicking a signature field. `0` - signer cannot decline, `1` - signer can decline.

Without this parameter, the signer receives the default SMS: "SignNow document invite unlock code: 123456". Requires an API free trial, an active API subscription, or a Site License.

put.description:
This endpoint allows API users to complete a document group correction and apply the new signers, documents, and invite settings. With this endpoint, you can:

* Change the signers and viewers of the document group
* Update the invite settings
* Reorder and remove documents that were not signed yet
* Add new documents to the document group

Before completing the correction, [initiate](/docs/document-group/operations/post-v2-document-groups-document-group-id-invite-document-group-invite-id-correction) it.

**Partially signed invites**

A recipient counts as having signed once they complete their signing action or fill in at least one field on any document in the group. The document does not need to be fully completed.

When some recipients have already signed:

* Add new signers and viewers to the last step that was at least partially signed, or to any later step. Earlier steps are locked.
* A recipient who already signed a document in the last signed step can be added to that step as a viewer of another document.
* The role of a recipient who already signed keeps its email address.

Steps that were cancelled when the correction started are recreated when you complete it:

* If the last signed step is complete, the next step's invites are sent right away. Adding only viewers to the completed step does not change this.
* If you add a signer to the last completed step, the step returns to pending. The next step's invites are sent once the new signer finishes.

*For example*, an invite has three steps, and steps 1 and 2 are signed. You can add new signers to steps 2 and 3. If you add a signer to step 2, step 3's invites are sent after that signer completes step 2.

post.description:
This endpoint allows API users to put a document group invite into correction mode. After that, [complete the correction](/docs/document-group/operations/put-v2-document-groups-document-group-id-invite-document-group-invite-id-correction) to change the signers, documents, and invite settings.

A correction can be initiated after some recipients have already signed. When the correction starts:

* Invites in steps that are not yet completed are cancelled. Pending recipients cannot access the documents until the correction is completed.
* Completed steps and everything already signed are kept and locked.

**Notes**

* The invite must be in `pending` status.
* A document group cannot be corrected if:
    * the invite includes a guest signer who wasn't sent a short link, an approver, or an SMS invite,
    * the invite is embedded or includes email groups,
    * the document group was declined or is already in correction mode,
    * the document group contains multirole or conditional fields,

post.description:
This endpoint allows API users to share a document group with a user by email, assigning them a specified role. If the user does not have an account, one is created automatically.

**Notes**

* **Viewer** - can view, download, and make copies of documents in a document group; **sender** - can view, download, make copies, invite to sign, and manage document invites.
* Only the owner of the document group can share it.
* A document group can be shared only once with the same user. Attempting to share again (even with a different role) returns an error.
* The user receives an email notification about the shared document group, including a preview link.
* If the user does not exist in the system, a new account is created automatically.
* If the document group was created from a document group template (DGT) that is already shared with the target user (as owner or sender), the sharing is rejected with a conflict error.

This endpoint allows API users to share a document group template with a user by email, assigning them a specified role. If the user does not have an account, one is created automatically.

**Notes**

* **Viewer** - can view, download, and make copies of documents in a document group template; **sender** - can view, download, make copies, invite to sign, and manage document invites.

* A document group template can be shared only once with the same user. Attempting to share again (even with a different role) returns an error.

* If the user does not exist in the system, a new account is created automatically.

post.summary: Create document group embedded view link
post.description:
This endpoint allows users to create an embedded view link for the specified document group. The link opens the document group in embedded view mode, enabling users to review and download documents without logging in to SignNow. Embedded view links can only be generated for documents and document groups.

**Additional information**

- Authentication is not required to open the link.
- The link can be used multiple times until it expires.
- The link can be generated for a document group in any status (e.g., waiting for others, signed, etc.).

You can customize the view mode experience in the editor and on the **You’ve viewed a document** page. Available options include:

- Set a custom logo in the editor and on the **You’ve viewed a document** page using `logo.url`.
- Customize the **Download Document** button style on the **You’ve viewed a document** page using `general.buttons.secondary`.
- Show or hide the **More Actions** menu in the editor using `settings.visibility`.
- Show or hide the **Close** button in the editor using `close-button.visibility`.
- Show or hide the **Download Document** button in the editor using `download-button.visibility`.
- Show or hide the sidebar navigation buttons in the editor using `icons`.
- Show or hide the **Download Document** button on the **You’ve viewed a document** page using `complete-page.button-download.visibility`. 

Learn more about [branding](/docs/guides-branding#about-branding).

parameters.description: Document group ID.

redirect_uri.description: The link that opens after a user clicks the **Close** button. If not set, the default page **You’ve viewed a document** page will be used.

get.description:
This endpoint allows API users to retrieve the details of a folder, including its subfolders and the documents it contains. Use query parameters to filter, sort, and paginate the document list.

**Notes**

* `total_documents` is the total number of documents in the folder. The `documents` array contains only the page selected by `limit` and `offset`.
* To include document group templates, set `entity_type` to `dgt` or `all`. By default, a templates folder returns only templates.
* Each document's `document_group_template_info` lists the active document group templates that include it. For a document that isn't part of any document group template, the array is empty.

parameters.name: folder_id
parameters.description: ID of the folder to return.

parameters.name: filter-values
parameters.description: Value for the filter set in `filters`. For `filters=signing-status`, one of: `signed`, `pending`, `waiting-for-me`, `waiting-for-others`, `unsent`, `expired`. For `filters=documents-created` or `filters=documents-updated`, a Unix timestamp: the response includes documents created or updated after this time.

parameters.name: sortby
parameters.description: Field to sort documents by. Possible values: `updated`, `created`, `document-name`.

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: Order of sorting. Can be used only with `sortby`. Possible values: `asc`, `desc`.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Number of documents to skip before the returned page starts.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of documents to return. Max: `100`.

parameters.name: entity_type
parameters.description: Entities to include in the response. Possible values: `document-all` (documents, including documents in document groups), `document` (documents that aren't in document groups), `document-group` (document groups only), `template` (templates only), `dgt` (document group templates only), `all` (documents and document groups, or templates and document group templates in a templates folder).

parameters.name: entity_labels
parameters.description: Label to filter documents and document groups by. Possible values: `declined` (the invite was declined), `undelivered` (the invite email wasn't delivered). To use both, separate them with a comma: `declined,undelivered`.

parameters.name: filters
parameters.description: Filter to apply to the document list. Possible values: `signing-status`, `documents-created`, `documents-updated`. Use with `filter-values`. The `documents-created` and `documents-updated` filters exclude templates.

parameters.name: include_documents_subfolders
parameters.description: Whether to include subfolders to the response. Allowed values: `1`, `0`.

parameters.name: with_team_documents
parameters.description: Whether to display Team Documents folders.

parameters.name: only_favorites
parameters.description: Whether to show only favorite documents and document groups.

* With document group where user is the owner (+email group)

get.description:
This endpoint allows API users to get the root folder of the user and its top-level folders, including the system folders (`Documents`, `Archive`, `Templates`, `Trash Bin`) and team folders.

**Notes**

* The same operation is also available at `GET /folder`.
* `document_count` and `template_count` depend on `entity_type`. By default (`document-all`), a folder counts only documents or only templates, depending on the folder type.
* To get the contents of a specific folder, call `GET /folder/{folder_id}`.

parameters.name: filters
parameters.description: Filter to apply to the document list. Possible values: `signing-status`, `documents-created`, `documents-updated`. Set the filter value in `filter-values`.

parameters.name: filter-values
parameters.description: Value for the filter set in `filters`. For `signing-status`: `signed`, `pending`, `waiting-for-me`, `waiting-for-others`, `unsent`. For `documents-created` and `documents-updated`: a Unix timestamp; documents created or updated from that time are returned. Date filters do not apply to templates.

parameters.name: sortby
parameters.description: Field to sort documents by. Possible values: `created`, `updated`, `recently_used`. `recently_used` sorts templates by the date the last invite was sent and applies to `Templates` folders.

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: Sort order. Can be used only with `sortby`. Possible values: `desc`, `asc`. Default: `desc`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of documents to return. Max: `100`. Larger values are reduced to `100`.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Number of documents to skip before the returned page starts.

parameters.name: subfolder-data
parameters.description: Whether to include subfolders in the response. Possible values: `1`, `0`. Must be used with `include_documents_subfolders`.

parameters.name: include_documents_subfolders
parameters.description: Whether to include subfolders in the response. Possible values: `1`, `0`. Must be used with `subfolder-data`.

parameters.name: with_team_documents
parameters.description: Whether to include `Team Documents` folders. Possible values: `true`, `false`.

parameters.name: only_favorites
parameters.description: Whether to return only favorite documents and document groups. Possible values: `true`, `false`. Default: `false`.

parameters.name: entity_type
parameters.description: Entities counted in `document_count` and `template_count`. Possible values: `document-all` (default): only documents or only templates, depending on the folder type. `all`: all entity types in the folder. `document`: documents that are not in a document group; `Documents`, `Archive`, and `Trash Bin` folders only. `document-group`: documents in document groups; `Documents`, `Archive`, and `Trash Bin` folders only. `template`: templates; `Templates` and `Trash Bin` folders only. `dgt`: document group templates; `Templates` and `Trash Bin` folders only.

200.description:
* Success
* With document group invite where user is the owner
* With document group invite where user is the signer
* With viewer field invites

get.description:
This endpoint allows API users to retrieve all brands associated with their account.

**Notes**

Each brand has an `owner_type` field that defines who owns it and what access is allowed. There are three ownership types:

* **`common`** — system default SignNow brand. Read-only; cannot be edited or customized. Appears in the brand list, but any modification attempt returns a "No access to brand" error.
* **`organization`** — custom brand owned by the organization. Full access for organization admins. This is the brand type customers should create and use.
* **`user`** — custom brand owned by an individual user.

* At least one brand was created.

count.description: Number of brands on the current page.

next.description: Link to the next page. Present only if there are more pages.

links.description: Pagination links. Empty array `[]` if on the last page. Object with `next` key if more pages exist.

post.description:
This endpoint allows users to upload a template in JSON/XML file with brand settings and current resources.

Get the up-to-date template file [here](/docs/general-branding/operations/get-v2-brands-template-file). 

Assign the created brand ID to any of these levels: 

* [Brand your documents](/docs/general-branding/operations/put-v2-documents-document-id-brand). 
* [Brand your document groups](/docs/general-branding/operations/put-v2-document-groups-document-group-id-brand). 
* [Brand your applications](/docs/general-branding/operations/put-v2-applications-application-id-brand). 
 
The template structure consists of two required objects: 

* `title`: a string parameter with a brand title. 
* `resources`: an array of objects with the list of resources and their properties. 

Example schema:

```
{
    "title": "some brand title",
    "resources": [
        "general": {...},
        "editor": {...},
        "send-invite": {...},
        "logo": {...},
        "email-general": {...},
        "email-invite": {...},
        ...
    ]
}

```

get.description:
This endpoint allows API users to retrieve the list of events the user account is subscribed to.

The results can be filtered and sorted. If the `sort` parameter is not indicated, the results are sorted by the `created` parameter in descending order. The `filters` and `sort` parameters need URL-encoding.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: In how many pages to display the response.

parameters.name: sort:created
parameters.description: Sort results by the date. Possible values: asc, desc. Format: `?sort[created]=desc`

parameters.name: sort:event
parameters.description: Sort results by the event type (from A to Z). Possible values: asc, desc. Format: `?sort[event]=desc`

parameters.name: sort:application
parameters.description: Sort results by the application name (from A to Z). Possible values: asc, desc. Format: `?sort[application]=desc`

parameters.name: filters:entity_id, callback_url
parameters.description: Search for a string in entity IDs and callback URLs. Format: `?filters=[{"_OR":[{"entity_id":{"type":"like","value":"21a28b47"}},{"callback_url":{"type":"like","value":"21a28b47"}}]}]`

parameters.name: filters:date
parameters.description: Filter results by the timestamps. Format: `?filters=[{"date":{"type":"between","value":[1580719773,1580720509]}}]`

parameters.name: filters:event
parameters.description: Filter results by the specific type of event. Format: `?filters=[{"event":{"type": "in", "value":["document.create", "document.update"]}}]`

parameters.name: filters:application
parameters.description: Filter results by the application. Format: `?filters=[{"application":{"type": "in", "value":["applicationUniqueId1", "applicationUniqueId2"]}}]`

parameters.name: Content-Type
parameters.description: application/json

post.description:
This endpoint allows users to subscribe an external service (`callback_url`) to a specific event related to a user, document, or document group. When the subscribed event occurs, your service receives a notification.

See the full list of available events in the [Webhooks user guide](/docs/guides-webhooks#entity-events).
Use [HMAC verification](/docs/guides-webhooks#hmac-security) for an additional layer of security.

> [!NOTE]
> For the payload your service receives for each event, see the response examples in [Get callback info by ID](/docs/callbacks-info/operations/get-v2-dashboard-event-subscriptions-subscription-id-callbacks).

event.description: Event name that triggers the subscription. Check [list of events](/docs/guides-webhooks#entity-events).

entity_id.description: Unique string ID of the entity (e.g., `document_id`, `user_id`, `document_group_id`).

delay.description: Delay in seconds before the webhook is sent after the event triggers.

headers.description: Custom HTTP headers to be sent with the callback request (e.g., Authorization tokens).

callback.description: URL that receives the event callback.

secret_key.description: Secret key used to generate the HMAC signature for verifying request authenticity.

use_tls_12.description: Whether TLS 1.2 should be used for the callback request.

retry_count.description: Maximum number of retries if the webhook fails with a 5xx error.

integration_id.description: Optional unique ID to identify the external system integration.

docid_queryparam.description: Whether the document ID is included as a query parameter in the callback URL.

include_metadata.description: Whether document metadata is included in the callback payload.

delete_access_token.description: If `true`, the access token is removed from the webhook payload for security. Default is `true`.

post.description:
This endpoint generates an access token for a user.

In the request, specify the `grant_type` to use:

- `password`: generate an access token using the [password grant](/docs/authentication#password-grant).

- `refresh_token`: generate an access token using the [refresh token grant](/docs/authentication#refresh-token-grant).

Endpoint allows you to search through the documents of users of the organization. Available only to the Administrator of the organization. 

The `filters` query parameter is array of optional filter parameters. At least one filter must be added.

**Pay attention**: emails must be encoded in such format `sample_name%40email.com`

parameters.name: filters:text
parameters.description: Searches documents by the text in their text fields. Example: `?filters=[{"text":{"type":"=","value":"Some sample text"}}]`

parameters.name: filters:status
parameters.description: Searches documents by document status. Possible values: `waiting_for_signing`, `signed`, `pending_payment`. Example: `?filters=[{"status":{"type":"=","value":"signed"}}]`

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number of the search results. Min: `1`. Example: `?page=3`

parameters.name: sort:name
parameters.description: Sorts documents by document name. Possible values: `asc`, `desc`. Example: `?sort[name]=asc`

parameters.name: sort:added

get.description:
This endpoint allows API users to retrieve all brands associated with an organization.

**Notes**

Each brand has an `owner_type` field that defines who owns it and what access is allowed. There are two ownership types returned by this endpoint:

* **`common`** — system default SignNow brand. Read-only; cannot be edited or customized. Appears in the brand list, but any modification attempt returns a "No access to brand" error.
* **`organization`** — custom brand owned by the organization. Full access for organization admins. This is the brand type you should create and use for customization.
